title: ensures with result
concept: The result keyword in ensures clauses lets you verify properties of the return value — correctness baked into the function signature.
why: Without result-checking ensures, you'd need separate tests for every return value property. With ensures, the check runs on every call.
tips: Think of ensures: result >= min as "I promise the return value is at least min"
Use result liberally — it turns your function into a self-documenting specification
Combine result checks with @pre to verify state transitions
If your ensures uses result and fails, the bug is in your implementation
common_mistakes: Writing circular ensures like ensures: result == f(result) — must be verifiable
Forgetting to add ensures when refactoring a function
